assessment.summary: TREM2 is a well-characterized immunoreceptor with excellent structural coverage (15 PDB entries, best at 1.47Å, 11 with bound ligands), confirming a druggable extracellular binding site. Despite zero ChEMBL IC50 entries, a 2026 first-in-human trial of an oral small-molecule agonist (VG-3927/SAR448851) demonstrates real chemical tractability not yet captured in public databases. Strong disease validation in Alzheimer's disease and cancer immunology, combined with emerging clinical-stage chemistry, supports a medium-to-high druggability assessment.
evidence_gaps: Zero ChEMBL IC50 entries despite apparent small-molecule activity — public chemical data severely lags behind the field
No approved drugs; clinical-stage compound (VG-3927/SAR448851) has not yet demonstrated efficacy in humans
Mechanism of small-molecule agonism of TREM2 not fully characterised in the public domain
AlphaFold coverage of transmembrane and intracellular signalling domains is lower confidence (pLDDT <70 for ~39% of residues)
Selectivity profile of small-molecule TREM2 agonists versus related TREM family members not established in public data
Downstream pharmacodynamic biomarkers for TREM2 agonism in humans remain to be validated
